The test must fail when filtering is disconnected, the copied engine is wrong, ui/lib links remain self-anchors, or the no-JavaScript table omits rows or commands. No API replacement, request interception, view injection, canned clipboard value, or skipped target is accepted.

flows.actor: Visitor recovering from an unknown documentation URL
preconditions: Use the isolated candidate containing ORI-AST-009 and its existing dependencies ORI-AST-001, ORI-AST-004, and ORI-CONT-005.

Serve the current candidate's dist at http://localhost:4321. Confirm listener ownership before observation.
Record a fresh run ID and candidate source, lockfile, test-source, built-dist, Pagefind, surface-policy, and coldboot-policy hashes.

steps.action: Navigate to a fresh run-specific unknown path under /docs/. Capture the actual navigation response and inspect the custom missing-page title, explanation, search hint, header, footer, and recovery links against the real system manuscript.
Inspect the emitted 404.html and its served recovery content. Confirm that the system manuscript remains outside the docs collection and does not create an ordinary documentation navigation entry.
Activate Search the site from the recovery page. Measure activation-to-dialog visibility separately from Pagefind readiness and inspect the focused input.

Await the real index, search for message, select the actual Message result with the keyboard, and navigate to /components/message. Observe dialog closure, the navigation response, the final URL, and substantive Message content.
Return to a fresh unknown path, reopen search, and dismiss it with Escape. Verify focus returns to the actual recovery-page invoking control.

Open search from an ordinary page and compare its actual module/index resources and Message destination with recovery-page search. Query the missing-page title and a distinctive phrase from the actual system manuscript; inspect returned result URLs and verify the missing-page document is excluded.
Set the site theme through its real existing control, revisit an unknown path, and inspect the retained theme and shared header/footer. Do not write theme state directly from the test.

In the JavaScript-disabled context, navigate to a fresh unknown path. Read the missing-page explanation and follow the plain Components and Registry links, observing HTTP 200 responses and matching rendered destination content.

observable_expected: A genuinely unknown path displays the candidate's custom recovery document with the actual manuscript content, rather than an empty shell or an unrelated page.
The build emits 404.html, while system/not-found.md remains outside the docs collection and ordinary documentation navigation.
The existing native search dialog has aria-modal=true, becomes visible within 300ms of activation independently of index readiness, and focuses its actual input.
The real Message result closes the dialog and reaches /components/message with HTTP 200 and substantive Message content.
Escape restores focus to the actual recovery-page search trigger.
Recovery and ordinary-page search use the same production Pagefind resources and real Message destination. Neither 404.html nor the run-specific unknown URL appears as a search result.
The existing site theme, header, and footer remain present on the custom recovery page.
Without JavaScript, the missing-page explanation remains readable and plain Components and Registry links reach real matching content.
Observed /components/message, /components, and /registry destinations and their rendered content are success targets. Generic roots and static success markers cannot satisfy the proof.
Local preview observations do not substitute for the separate deployed Worker HTTP 404 status-code proof.
evidence_capture: Current-run source, lockfile, test-source, dist, Pagefind, and policy identities plus actual build output.
Unknown-path navigation response, emitted 404.html identity, and rendered system-copy observations.
Dialog-open timing, focused-element observations, keyboard navigation, and restored-focus observations.
Actual search-resource URLs, result URLs, response statuses, and destination-content observations.
Browser traces and screenshots of enhanced recovery, retained theme, and JavaScript-disabled Components and Registry navigation.
teardown: Dismiss any open dialog, detach observers, and close only this run's browser contexts.
Stop only the preview process launched and recorded by this run.
Retain current-run evidence and release only owned scratch resources.

flows.red_proof_contract: Run the exact command against a recorded preimplementation candidate with a functioning real build, preview, and prerequisite search implementation. Capture an actual assertion failure for missing recovery behavior through the governing run_flow RED capture format at proof.red. Missing infrastructure, unmatched tests, source absence alone, or an authored success flag cannot establish RED. The assertions must fail for a generic missing-page shell, disconnected recovery search, broken destination links, or an indexed 404 document. Do not intercept requests, inject recovery markup, manufacture results, or skip browser targets.

flows.desc: Prove the already-planned example API integration before screen composition: real OpenAI streaming, SDK-produced conversation history, request validation, configuration rejection, upstream failure, active cancellation, recovery, actual package compatibility and owned-process cleanup.

preconditions: Use the isolated ORI-AI-001 candidate and its unchanged existing dependencies. This proof requires no Quickstart page, ORI-CONT-004 output, native screen or ORI-AI-002 output.
Verify the actual pinned packages through the preserved setup commands. Missing or incompatible packages, credentials, networking or model access fail closed.

Reserve the actual backend address and port. Launch the real Node server through the task-owned backend lifecycle and record PID, launch identity, source and lockfile hashes, test and policy hashes, commands and a fresh run ID.
Pass OPENAI_API_KEY only to the trusted launcher and real server child. Keep credentials out of installs, compilers, client configuration, command arguments and captured evidence.
Use the fixed official OpenAI endpoint, the primary model, maxOutputTokens=1024, maxRetries=0 and the bounded request deadline already required by ORI-AI-001.
Materialize the API-specific governed surface policy supplied in this payload before task-plan validation.

steps.action: Run the exact flow-ID-selected integration suite against the real owned server. Submit a fresh nonce-bearing text prompt through POST /api/chat and consume actual SDK UI-stream deltas.
Submit a contextual follow-up using the SDK-produced first-turn history, including assistant structural parts. Do not repeat the nonce in the second user message.

Exercise malformed and prohibited input, the 64 KiB body limit, the 50-message limit, unsupported methods, missing or malformed configuration, and an occupied port. Pair rejection evidence with a real successful request.
Restart the same real server with a deliberately nonexistent model, observe the actual provider rejection, restore the primary model and verify successful recovery.
Abort a real unfinished HTTP stream after observing a delta. Verify provider cancellation and resource cleanup, then complete another real request.
Execute the preserved package, server-compiler, scoped hook-compiler and lint checks. Inspect the actual client import boundary and clean up all recorded server children.

observable_expected: A valid request produces at least two nonempty text deltas before completion, with actual response ID, model, usage, request correlation and final text hash.
The contextual answer includes the first turn's nonce even though the second user message omits it.
Invalid bodies return 400, oversized bodies return 413 and unsupported methods return 405; rejected input causes zero provider calls.
Invalid startup configuration exits before listening. An occupied port does not cause another listener to be killed or silently substituted.
The real rejected-model request produces a sanitized failure; restoring the primary model produces a real completed response.
Cancellation occurs while generation is unfinished, reaches the provider AbortController and releases resources. Ordinary completed request-body close does not abort generation.
The actual pinned SDK and hook import graph compile without compatibility shims, replacement declarations or weakened compiler settings.
The run records exact source, command, outcome and teardown evidence. Scoped compiler success does not claim rendered hook acceptance or whole-example correctness.
evidence_capture: run.json containing current-run identity, source/lockfile/test/policy hashes, exact command and exit, and references to the actual ORI-AI-001 package, provider-stream, error-abort, validation and teardown artifacts.
Timestamped nonempty stream deltas, actual final answer, nonce/history correlation, request IDs, provider response IDs, configured model, usage and terminal outcomes.
Observed validation responses, provider-call counts for rejected requests, invalid-launch exits, genuine upstream rejection, active cancellation and restored successful requests.
proof.red captured by run_flow.py with --expect red for the exact locked command; its header and command hash must remain intact.
red.txt retained as the requested supplementary transcript of that same actual RED run. It is not the validator's canonical red_proof.

Never author success receipts, substitute a provider, replay a canned stream or introduce artificial stream delays.
teardown: Abort unfinished requests and clear request deadlines and listeners on success, failure, disconnect and shutdown.
Stop only server children identified by this run's owned backend handles; preserve unrelated listeners.
Restore the primary model after rejected-model testing and record actual stop/restart outcomes.
Verify that every recorded child has exited and no owned listener or active generation remains.

scenario.verification_service: Real Node 24 example HTTP server, installed AI SDK v7 packages and OpenAI Responses API at https://api.openai.com/v1 using gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14

start_state.description: Launch the actual server through its CLI in the isolated candidate using valid server-only configuration; reserve its port and record its PID, source identity and a fresh nonsecret run nonce.
records: OPENAI Responses model=gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14; official base URL fixed
Empty new conversation; 0 assistant turns; fresh nonce generated for this invocation

would_fail_if: The HTTP route is a static success response or is disconnected from the real provider.
History is omitted or the SDK-produced assistant step-start parts are rejected.
Input validation is a no-op, secrets are logged, or normal request-body close incorrectly aborts generation.
The provider AbortController is disconnected from HTTP cancellation or teardown leaves owned listeners active.
The hook uses a stub transport or incompatible SDK declarations instead of the installed packages.

steps: POST a fresh DefaultChatTransport envelope to /api/chat containing a text prompt asking for the current nonce followed by a substantive explanation; consume the actual SDK UI stream incrementally.
Send a second turn containing the SDK-produced first-turn history, including its assistant structural parts; ask for the earlier marker without repeating the nonce in the new user message.

must_observe: At least 2 nonempty text deltas arrive before terminal completion; concatenation contains the current run nonce.
The second answer contains the exact `runNonce` from the first turn, although the second user message omits it.
Both responses carry actual provider response IDs, model, usage, request IDs, text hashes and terminal outcome: completed.
must_not_observe: 0 assistant deltas, empty response, or a static canned answer.
A second request without first-turn history or an HTTP 200 stream classified successful after an error.

steps: Send malformed JSON, invalid envelopes, system/tool/file parts and client provider/model overrides to /api/chat.
Send a body exceeding 65536 bytes, an envelope with 51 messages, and an unsupported method; retain a valid text request as the positive control.

must_observe: Invalid bodies and 51-message input return HTTP 400; oversized body returns HTTP 413; unsupported method returns HTTP 405.
Each rejected request has recorded provider-call count=0; the positive control receives a real completed provider stream.
must_not_observe: HTTP 200 or provider dispatch for rejected input; empty rejection evidence.

steps: Launch actual server children with each required configuration value missing or malformed and with an occupied reserved port, preserving the existing listener.
Launch again with valid configuration and send a real request.

must_observe: Every invalid launch has exit_code > 0 before listening; occupied-port handling preserves the recorded original PID.
The restored valid launch answers `/api/chat` with a real completed provider response.
must_not_observe: A server listening after configuration rejection, hidden port substitution, or empty launch diagnostics.

steps: Restart the actual owned server with a deliberately nonexistent model identifier while retaining the official provider endpoint and real credential.
Send valid text input, observe the actual provider rejection and sanitized HTTP or SDK stream failure, then restore the primary model and repeat.

must_observe: The nonexistent model produces an actual upstream rejection with terminal outcome: `error` and a sanitized client-visible error.
Restored gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14 produces a completed real response with usage and response ID.
must_not_observe: An empty error record, leaked credentials/raw provider error, fallback model, or error stream counted as successful.

steps: Request a long bounded response and abort the real HTTP request after observing a delta while generation remains unfinished.
Observe the server's abort and cleanup, then issue a new independent real request.
Treat completion before cancellation as nondiscriminating and retry with a longer bounded prompt; never delay the stream artificially.

must_observe: The unfinished request records outcome=aborted and provider cancellation; its active-generation count returns to 0.
The subsequent request produces at least 2 real deltas and outcome: completed; normal request-body close does not abort generation.
must_not_observe: No cancellation signal, continued orphan generation, or a completed-before-Stop run accepted as abort evidence.

steps: Run the preserved package-list, server compiler and scoped live-chat compiler commands against actual installed dependencies; run the scoped lint command.
Inspect the real hook/config import graph and verify server credentials and provider imports remain unreachable from client code.
Stop all recorded server children and inspect their ports and shutdown outcomes.

must_observe: The real server and scoped hook compilers exit 0 with the pinned packages and no replacement declarations.
The actual hook uses stable DefaultChatTransport, expo/fetch, throttle: 50, empty initial messages and validated absolute API configuration.
After teardown, owned active requests: 0; owned listeners: 0; all recorded server children have exited.
must_not_observe: Empty compiler evidence, compatibility shims, client credential reads, skipped dependencies or a leftover owned listener.
A scoped compiler result presented as rendered useChat acceptance or whole-example/gallery success.
